sentence: This project studies cerebellar physiological differences among patients with essential tremor and uses machine learning to sort them into subtypes.
This project tries to find out how food insecurity affects glycemic control and health care utilization in youth and young adults with diabetes.
This project studies the roots of allergies and immune system diseases in children and looks for possible treatments.
This project tries to find out how fractionated photoimmunotherapy can treat advanced or recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer, using experiments and mathematical models.
This project builds methods that find where two transcription factors bind genomic DNA in human cancers and which partners bind with them.
This project studies how somatic mosaicism differs across the colon in colorectal cancer and inflammatory bowel disease.
This project builds therapies for leiomyosarcoma that target a DNA damage response enzyme, and tests low-dose doxorubicin in a clinical trial.
This project tests possible treatments for congenital muscular dystrophy using mouse and patient-derived cellular models.
This project tries to advance a small molecule that switches on a silenced paternal allele in neurons as a treatment for Angelman syndrome.
This project uses deep reinforcement learning with single cell omics and real world data to find drug targets and repurposable drugs for Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how a transcription factor made by Epstein-Barr virus regulates transcription.
This project builds statistical models and computational tools that combine viral genome sequencing and phenotyping to study how viruses spread in outbreaks.
This project tests how a virus-like particle vaccine with added adjuvants works and studies the adaptive immune response in murine and non-human primate models.
This project studies how cellular proteins move nutrient transporters between the plasma membrane and the endosome, with a focus on copper handling.
This project collects long-term follow-up data and biospecimens from participants through chart review and annual surveys.
This project tests whether MRI of glycolysis, perfusion and cell death can predict how bladder cancer models respond to immunotherapy.
This project builds a way to group neurologically intact people across the lifespan into motor phenotypes using multimodal data.
This project studies what drives ependymoma, focusing on biomolecular condensates and their effect on gene transcription and tumorigenesis.
This project studies how to make cardiovascular care less variable and better in quality.
This project studies how RNA nanoparticles expressed in muscle and liver shape immunity, to design RNA that boosts immunity or tolerance.
